questions.question:
Read this email from your English-speaking friend Sam and the notes you have made.

From: Sam
Subject: Maya's birthday

Hi!

It's Maya's birthday on the 18th and I'd love us to plan something special for her. [Note: Great idea!]

I was thinking of either a picnic in the park or going bowling. Which do you think she'd prefer? [Note: Say which and why]

I'd also like to buy her a present together with you. Have you got any ideas? [Note: Suggest...]

Could we meet this weekend to organise everything? [Note: Yes, tell Sam when]

Speak soon,
Sam

Write your email to Sam using all the notes. Write about 100 words.
questions.explanation: A good answer is an informal email (e.g. 'Hi Sam', 'See you soon') of about 100 words that covers all four notes: 1) reacts positively to the idea of doing something for Maya's birthday; 2) chooses the picnic or bowling and gives a reason (e.g. 'She'd prefer bowling because she loves games and it might rain'); 3) suggests a present (e.g. a book by her favourite author, concert tickets); 4) agrees to meet and says when (e.g. 'How about Saturday afternoon at the café?'). Content, communicative achievement, organisation (linking words such as because, so, also) and a range of B1 language (would, could, suggestions like 'Why don't we...?') are assessed. Missing a note lowers the Content mark.

questions.question:
Choose ONE of these questions. Write about 100 words.

Article
You see this notice on an English-language website for teenagers.

Articles wanted!
A celebration I will never forget
Tell us about a celebration you will always remember. What were you celebrating? Who was there? Why was it so special?
The best articles will appear on our website.

Write your article.

Story
Your English teacher has asked you to write a story. Your story must begin with this sentence:

Everyone shouted 'Surprise!' when I walked in.

Write your story.
questions.explanation: Article: a good answer has an interesting title or opening that catches the reader's attention, answers all three questions (what was celebrated, who was there, why it was special), gives some personal feelings or opinions, and speaks to the reader (e.g. 'Have you ever...?'). Story: a good answer begins with the given sentence, has a clear sequence of events and an ending, uses past tenses correctly (past simple, past continuous, past perfect), and includes some description of feelings (e.g. 'I couldn't believe my eyes'). For both, about 100 words; content, communicative achievement, organisation and a range of B1 language are assessed.
